55.subject: A single long halberd combines an oiled-steel crescent blade with a brass shaft mechanism whose exposed cartwheel mainspring sits just below the head. The spring is half-wound and pulls two copper tension rods taut along the blade spine, while a small arc-blue release stud marks the grip.
55.perspective: Clean diagonal three-quarter weapon portrait showing the complete head, mainspring, shaft, and grip inside the middle 70% with generous margin.
55.background: A warm parchment-amber armory wall with blurred wooden racks, opposing the cool steel blade and blue release stud.
55.notes: No wielder, readable markings, clock numerals, gun mechanism, oversized fantasy blade, lightning discharge, extra weapons, or cropped tip.

58.subject: A single compact polearm built to cut wind rather than flesh: a charcoal-black haft supports two offset storm-silver crescent vanes around an open center, where a taut cyan filament vibrates between gold-white contact points. A narrow ribbon of air passes through the gap and splits into two clean trails behind the head.
58.perspective: Diagonal three-quarter weapon portrait with the complete twin-vane head, vibrating filament, grip, and split air trails contained inside the middle 70%.
58.background: A warm dusty coral sky above a softly blurred cliff forge, separating the cool silver-black weapon and cyan focal filament.
58.notes: No wielder, readable marks, oversized axe blade, lightning explosion, tornado, extra weapons, cropped tip, or resemblance to Mainspring Halberd.

64.subject: A short single-edged dagger shown whole and in near-profile: a blade-silver blade with a hollow fuller running its full length, the fuller carrying a slow toxic-lime fluid that beads and hangs at the point. The grip is wrapped in shadow-black cord under a bone-white pommel cap, with a thin midnight purple-grey guard.
64.perspective: Near-orthographic profile, long lens, the entire weapon inside the frame and tilted only slightly off vertical, dead-centred.
64.background: A flat warm amber-brown ground with a soft ochre falloff and no scene at all, so the cold silver and the toxic lime separate cleanly at icon size.
64.notes: The object alone: no hand, no wielder, no ground plane, no scene. Compact, never a long corner-to-corner diagonal. Whole weapon in frame with nothing that matters outside the inner 60 percent.

200.subject: Two differently armored hands meet over a cracked foundation stone: one in char-black forge leather and one in cool iron-grey mail, both gripping the same plain aged-bronze mason's clamp as it closes a repaired seam. A small warm lantern flame reflects equally on both wrists.
200.perspective: Tight top-down three-quarter close view with the joined hands, bronze clamp, and closing stone seam centered as one simple gesture.
200.background: A muted cool slate worktable with pale dust and soft blue shadow, allowing the warm skin, leather, bronze, and lantern reflection to separate.
200.notes: Show cooperation through the shared tool, not a handshake alone. No treaty text, signatures, flags, logos, crowd, weapons, magical aura, or political symbols.

201.subject: A broken black-stone gatehouse is being made defensible again as molten-orange forge seams join three major cracks and heavy bronze braces clamp the arch in place. A controlled line of ember-red light travels upward from a portable brazier to the repaired keystone.
201.perspective: Low wide three-quarter view focused on the single repaired gate arch, with its keystone, braces, and complete heated seam inside the middle 70%.
201.background: A cold pale-blue dawn sky and blue-grey distant rubble, providing clean contrast behind the char-black masonry and warm repair lines.
201.notes: Depict reconstruction, not a burning castle. No readable banners, armies, siege, lava moat, giant explosion, or full city panorama.

202.subject: One almost-dead coal in a cracked iron hearth opens from within, revealing a fresh molten-orange core as a small upright flame curls through the fracture. A ring of black ash peels back and three gold sparks rise, capturing renewal at its smallest decisive instant.
202.perspective: Macro low three-quarter close view with the single coal, fresh inner flame, and three sparks centered against generous negative space.
202.background: A cold desaturated blue stone hearth and soft grey ash bed, making the new orange flame the only warm element.
202.notes: Keep the event intimate and singular. No hands, phoenix, bonfire, fireplace room, runes, multiple coals, explosive burst, or human silhouette.

204.subject: A broken stone water channel closes as two narrow ribbons of deep-teal current weave through opposite cracks and meet beneath a pale moon-silver shell clasp. Seafoam gathers along the repaired joint, and a single clear stream begins flowing forward again.
204.perspective: Close top-down three-quarter view centered on the channel break, shell clasp, joining currents, and restored stream path.
204.background: Warm sun-baked ochre masonry and amber sand surround the cool water repair, providing direct hue and temperature opposition.
204.notes: No caster, hands, text, plumbing diagram, waterfall, flood, ice, or battlefield; the repair itself is the one readable event.

205.subject: A deep-teal tide pool and a warm stone settlement cistern meet through one newly opened saltwood sluice, their waters forming a clean seafoam spiral around a shared pale shell token. Two cropped hands, one weathered and one translucent with brine, steady the sluice from opposite sides.
205.perspective: Tight overhead three-quarter composition with the joined waters, shell token, sluice, and two hands centered as one cooperative mechanism.
205.background: Warm amber masonry on one side and cool blue-grey reef stone on the other, clearly separated yet balanced behind the central seafoam spiral.
205.notes: No written treaty, flags, handshake, full figures, whirlpool, giant wave, treasure, or romantic imagery.

206.subject: Three distinct deepwater currents—abyssal blue, deep teal, and pale moon-silver—rise from separate hollow shells and braid into one thick protective column around a small restored beacon stone. Bioluminescent points travel upward in coordinated spirals without forming creatures or faces.
206.perspective: Low close three-quarter view with the complete braided current column, three source shells, and beacon stone centered inside the middle 70%.
206.background: A warm copper-orange cavern shore lit by amber mineral glow, making the cold allied currents read with maximum contrast.
206.notes: Alliance is three currents joining, not three characters. No sea monster, tornado, portal, text, watery humanoids, flood, or uncontrolled spray.

207.subject: A dented iron-grey helm rests atop a folded bone-white burial cloth while one funerary-bronze bell clapper lies beside it and a green-gold soul filament rises in a single dignified arc. A warm human hand has just placed a small unmarked bronze token at the cloth's edge.
207.perspective: Tight eye-level tabletop three-quarter view with the helm, folded cloth, token, and full soul filament centered inside the frame.
207.background: A warm amber-lit memorial alcove of ochre stone fading into soft shadow, with the pale cloth and green-gold filament remaining distinct.
207.notes: Honor, not gore or triumph. No corpse, readable inscription, weapon display, wreath, flag, crowd, skull pile, or dramatic resurrection.

208.subject: Two bone-white mourning veils are tied together around a single funerary-bronze bell whose clapper glows faint green-gold, while two cropped hands hold opposite ends of one iron chain laid gently beneath it. The shared knot and still bell make grief visibly mutual and deliberate.
208.perspective: Close top-down three-quarter composition with the joined veils, silent bell, chain, and two hands centered as one restrained arrangement.
208.background: A warm dark-amber wooden memorial table with soft candle haze, contrasting with the pale cloth and cool iron chain.
208.notes: No text, signatures, wedding imagery, ringing motion, faces, corpse, blood, skulls, or supernatural crowd.

209.subject: Seven empty suits of iron-grey memorial armor rise upright in a wide ring as green-gold soul filaments descend from one suspended funerary bell and enter each chest in sequence. Bone-white burial cloths lift from the ground around the circle, but no bodies or faces are visible.
209.perspective: High three-quarter wide view centered on the suspended bell and complete armor ring, keeping every silhouette simple and subordinate to the shared pattern.
209.background: A warm amber dawn cemetery of muted ochre soil and low mist, opposing the cool metal and green-gold rebirth light.
209.notes: Orderly communal return, not horror. No skeleton army, open graves, corpses, explosion, portal, readable markers, giant central hero, or chaotic overlapping figures.

210.subject: A single charred vine wrapped around a broken stone column sends out one fresh forest-green shoot, then unfurls three pale yellow-green leaves in a clear upward sequence. Honey-gold sap glows only at the junction where old blackened wood becomes new growth.
210.perspective: Close vertical three-quarter view with the full charred-to-living transition, three leaves, and broken column centered inside the frame.
210.background: A cool desaturated slate wall and thin blue mist, making the new green leaves and warm sap the only vivid colors.
210.notes: One vine, one rebloom event. No caster, giant flower, face, forest explosion, runes, text, swarm of roots, or complete building overgrowth.

211.subject: Two different living branches—one smooth pale sapling and one dark thorned bough—curve toward each other and graft around a single honey-gold seed, producing one shared white-green blossom at the join. Their roots remain visibly separate below the union.
211.perspective: Tight eye-level close view centered on the grafted branches, glowing seed, shared blossom, and separate root bases.
211.background: A cool charcoal stone niche with soft blue shadow, providing high value contrast behind the warm seed and pale new flower.
211.notes: No hands, written contract, heart shape, wedding symbolism, faces, giant tree, wreath, or uncontrolled floral field.

212.subject: A concentrated wave of forest-green stems races across a cracked stone floor and erupts into one fan of pale new leaves and honey-gold pollen at the leading edge. The growth follows a clear curved path, splitting three paving stones without obscuring them under a jungle.
212.perspective: Low ground-level three-quarter view following the curved growth path toward the centered fan of leaves and pollen.
212.background: A cool blue-grey colonnade in deep shade, opposing the warm pollen and vivid green surge while keeping the silhouette uncluttered.
212.notes: No caster, creatures, giant flowers, whole forest, tornado, explosion, text-like vine patterns, or frame-filling pollen cloud.

213.subject: A blackened-steel tinker’s hand releases one tiny brass gear across a slanted copper game board toward two open sockets: one glowing arc blue and one dark. The gear balances briefly on its edge at the branching track, with a taut mainspring beneath the board ready to snap either way.
213.perspective: Tight top-down three-quarter close view centered on the rolling gear, forked mechanical track, two sockets, and visible mainspring.
213.background: A warm parchment-amber workbench fading into soft shadow, opposing the cool steel hand and blue active socket.
213.notes: Chance is mechanical uncertainty, not casino imagery. No dice, cards, coins, readable odds, text, faces, gambling table, or explosive failure.

214.subject: A single diagonal workshop conveyor carries three stages of the same compact construct chassis—bare steel frame, brass-plated torso, then arc-blue core installation—beneath precisely spaced copper tool gantries. The final core has just lit, creating a clear left-to-right sequence without a crowd.
214.perspective: High three-quarter view along the conveyor with all three assembly stages and the lit final core centered inside the middle 70%.
214.background: A dark cool slate factory floor with soft iron shadows, making the warm brass stages and blue focal core stand out.
214.notes: No humanoid workers, endless factory vista, army of finished robots, text, numbered stations, smoke plume, or chaotic overlapping machinery.

215.subject: Four articulated ivory-ceramic tools converge on one worn brass construct core, replacing its dull copper ring with a larger polished-steel ring as an arc-blue pulse travels through newly aligned contacts. Removed pieces rest in one orderly row below, making the upgrade visibly planned and reversible.
215.perspective: Close overhead three-quarter view with the core, four tools, new ring, and ordered removed parts centered as one precise operation.
215.background: A warm dark-amber repair mat with subtle parchment texture, contrasting with the cool steel upgrade and blue electrical pulse.
215.notes: No readable blueprint, diagrams, humanoid patient, giant explosion, magical rune circle, weapon, or scattered scrap.

216.subject: A plain bone-white ceramic mask hangs against a warm wall as one hair-thin blade-silver scratch crosses its lower edge and a toxic-lime droplet settles precisely at the line's endpoint. Midnight-purple shadow has begun closing around the mask from both sides, leaving the mark unavoidable but restrained.
216.perspective: Tight frontal close view with the complete mask, silver scratch, green droplet, and encroaching shadow centered in a simple composition.
216.background: A warm amber plaster wall lit by one off-frame lantern, opposing the cold pale mask and dark shadow.
216.notes: No skull, target reticle, written name, blood, victim body, assassin hand, weapon, rune, or large green poison splash.

217.subject: A taut blade-silver wire snaps a single dark wooden support pin in a precise quiet cut, causing a suspended iron counterweight to begin dropping out of frame. One black-gloved hand releases the wire while a toxic-lime wax bead on the severed pin identifies the prepared contract without text.
217.perspective: Tight side-on three-quarter close view centered on the wire, breaking pin, releasing hand, and first movement of the counterweight.
217.background: A warm amber-lit warehouse beam and ochre dust haze, providing strong contrast around the cold silver mechanism and black glove.
217.notes: Imply the kill through engineered consequence; show no victim, corpse, blood, written contract, crossbow, giant trap, explosion, or full assassin.

220.subject: A single flexible lash of gold-white lightning curves through the air from a small storm-silver grip, its cyan inner trace tightening into one sharp loop just before the tip snaps straight. Three evenly spaced thunder beads show the wave traveling along the energy without forming a weapon of solid metal.
220.perspective: Close side-on three-quarter action view with the grip, full looping lash, thunder beads, and straightening tip centered against negative space.
220.background: A warm muted terracotta wall and amber dust haze, maximizing contrast around the cold cyan and gold-white electrical curve.
220.notes: No wielder, victim, giant bolt, chain links, multiple lashes, explosion, text, or lightning filling the entire frame.

221.subject: A dense gold-white thunder ring collapses around one cyan vertical bolt at the instant it strikes a single iron capstone, kicking out three short storm-silver pressure arcs and a tight halo of charcoal dust. The impact remains compact and geometrically clear.
221.perspective: Low close three-quarter view with the capstone, complete vertical bolt, collapsing ring, and three pressure arcs centered.
221.background: A warm burnt-orange cliff face under dusty amber light, opposing the cold bright electrical impact.
221.notes: One strike on one object. No caster, enemy figure, battlefield destruction, branching chain targets, giant explosion, storm panorama, or text-like symbol.

222.subject: Three different storm-silver conductor staffs lean inward until their tips form a stable triangle, holding one hovering charcoal cloud core while separate cyan currents join into a gold-white thunder ring around it. Only three cropped gloved hands steady the shafts at the lower edge.
222.perspective: Low upward three-quarter close view centered on the triangular staff tips, cloud core, joined currents, and complete thunder ring.
222.background: A warm coral-and-amber twilight sky with thin ochre cloud, providing maximum contrast behind the cool apparatus and black core.
222.notes: No readable oath, full casters, lightning storm, giant portal, tornado, flags, creature face in the cloud, or overlapping extra staffs.

223.subject: A storm-tap lever of tarnished storm-silver and charcoal iron is slammed hard past its final notch by two gauntleted hands, and an electric gold-white arc jumps the opened coil and races up both forearms. The coil housing glows white along its seam and the gauntlet plates are already scorched soot-black across the knuckles.
223.perspective: Tight close three-quarter on the lever and the two hands, camera at the height of the mechanism, the arc filling the upper third.
223.background: A warm rust-brown and lantern-amber workshop wall of half-rebuilt brick and fresh timber scaffold, kept dim and warm so the cold arc-white separates hard from it.
223.notes: The cost of the overdraw must be visible in the scorching, not celebrated. No face, no full figure, no bolt in the sky, no gauge markings or numerals.

224.subject: One flat sheet of electric gold-white arc-light snaps horizontally across a rain-slick rebuilt street at knee height, thin charcoal thunder-rings blooming where it passes. Storm-silver sparks skitter off the wet cobbles and every standing puddle flares cyan for the instant the sheet crosses it.
224.perspective: Low wide eye-level looking straight down the street so the flash reads as one long horizontal band across the whole frame.
224.background: Warm ochre and rust-brown terraced house fronts with lit torches and timber scaffolding, held dull and warm behind the cold flash.
224.notes: A brief WIDE flash, thin and fast and shallow, never one thick heroic bolt and never a landscape catastrophe. No figures, no crater, no burning buildings.

225.subject: A descending column of stormcloud-black drops four separate electric gold-white bolts at once into a rebuilt courtyard, the bolts braided with cyan double-traces and ringed by expanding charcoal thunder-rings. The strike points burn white and the courtyard flagstones are lifting.
225.perspective: Wide slightly low three-quarter across the courtyard, framed so the whole braided strike and its outermost thunder-ring sit inside the image.
225.background: A warm amber-lit settlement wall and its scaffolding beyond the courtyard, lit torches and thin warm ember-snow, kept far lower in value than the strike.
225.notes: The storm itself is the subject: no hero, caster, or named figure anywhere in frame. Keep it a strike on ONE courtyard, not a burning city and not a landscape-wide apocalypse.

226.subject: A figure caught mid-dissolve: the near half still solid in shadow-black leather and blade-silver buckles, the far half already unravelling into midnight purple-grey shadow-smoke that streams sideways and stops at a hard vanishing edge, leaving a faint bone-white outline where the body was.
226.perspective: Medium three-quarter at close eye level, framed so the dissolving edge runs through the centre of the image.
226.background: A warm amber torchlit alley of half-rebuilt brick and fresh timber scaffold, its light still falling on the patch of ground where the figure no longer is.
226.notes: The disappearance is the subject, and the torchlight landing on empty ground is what sells it. No face detail, no portal, no swirling magic circle, no second figure.

227.subject: A long braided lash of shadow-black cord tipped with blade-silver barbs snaps taut through the frame, flinging a spray of discrete toxic-lime venom droplets off its length. The barbs are already wet and the droplets hang bright and separate against the dark.
227.perspective: Medium close with the camera near the arc of the lash so it reads as one continuous S-curve across the frame, the barbed tip nearest the viewer.
227.background: A warm ochre and lantern-amber rebuilt wall, low in value and warm so the lime spray separates hard from it.
227.notes: The lash and its spray only: no wielder, no victim, no corpse. Keep the venom as bright discrete droplets, never a green fog or a haze.

228.subject: A single fist-sized chunk of granite-grey masonry with a rusted-bronze wall cramp still pinned through it, caught in flight just after release and trailing pale quartz dust with two smaller fragments tumbling behind. The mass and the spin read plainly on it.
228.perspective: Tight close three-quarter tracking alongside the stone at its own height, with motion blur only in the background and the stone itself sharp.
228.background: A warm ochre and ember-orange dusk sky above a half-rebuilt wall, kept warm and bright so the cold grey stone reads dark against it.
228.notes: ONE thrown chunk, fist-sized, plus two small fragments - not a boulder and not an avalanche. No thrower, no arm or hand in frame, no impact and no crater.

229.subject: A warden's gauntlet of rusted bronze and iron-black presses a flat granite-grey oath-stone into a half-repaired wall, and pale quartz light runs out from under the palm along every mortar seam in both directions, stitching the courses together. Moss-green creeps into the newly lit seams.
229.perspective: Tight three-quarter close on the gauntlet and the oath-stone, the lit seams running out of frame to both sides.
229.background: Warm lantern-amber and ember-orange torchlight falling on the timber scaffold standing against the wall.
229.notes: A vow made by one hand on stone, not a shouted rally: a single gesture. No face, no full figure, no banner, no crowd, and no written runes or lettering of any kind.

230.subject: A hinged brass-cornered strongbox stands flipped open on a workbench, its felt-lined trays packed with graded polished-brass gears, tarnished-copper mainsprings and tightly rolled parchment-amber blueprints. Two of the blueprint rolls have been lifted clear of the tray and stand proud of the box, arc-blue light waking along their cut edges.
230.perspective: Close top-down three-quarter over the open box, the box filling most of the frame with the two lifted rolls nearest the camera.
230.background: A deep cool slate-blue workshop shadow going nearly black at the corners, so the warm brass and parchment amber carry all of the light.
230.notes: TWO items lifted clear of the rest is the read. No hands, no figure, no coins or treasure hoard, and no lettering or diagrams legible on the blueprints.

231.subject: A palm-sized module of oiled steel and polished brass with a stacked pale-quartz prism at its heart is snapped into a socket and locking home. One thin arc-blue beam enters it and leaves as three brighter parallel beams, each fanning wider and hotter than the single beam that went in.
231.perspective: Tight three-quarter close on the module seated in its socket, the input beam entering at the left edge and the three output beams running off the right.
231.background: A deep cool slate-blue interior falling off to near-black, so the brass body and the arc-blue beams both separate.
231.notes: One beam in, THREE brighter out - the multiplication is the entire idea. No hands, no figure, no rainbow spectrum, no shattered glass.

1121.subject: A young settlement scout in a patched stone-grey coat steps through a newly cleared archway, carrying a short aged-bronze spyglass and a bundle of moss-green survey stakes. One warm lantern hangs low at the hip while a salvaged shoulder plate bears visible hammer dents but no emblem.
1121.perspective: Eye-level full-body three-quarter view with the scout's complete silhouette, spyglass, and forward step centered inside the middle 70%.
1121.background: A pale blue-grey dawn over roofless ruins and cool mist, separating the warm lantern and bronze tools from the open setting.
1121.notes: Keep the scout practical and lightly equipped, with no bow, military uniform, readable map, banner, heroic pose, or distant crowd.

1122.subject: A road-worn courier leans into a steady run, one hand protecting a sealed bronze message tube strapped across a moss-green sash while the other steadies a lantern-amber signal pennant folded tightly around its staff. The figure wears mixed settlement leathers repaired with two visibly different stitching styles.
1122.perspective: Low side-on three-quarter action view with the entire running courier, sealed tube, and folded pennant contained in the central composition.
1122.background: A cool rain-washed causeway between dark grey ruins under a pale sky, opposing the warm bronze tube and amber cloth.
1122.notes: The pennant stays folded and carries no emblem or text. No horse, army, open letter, sprinting crowd, royal costume, or combat scene.

1123.subject: A repaired settlement barricade construct stands on two blocky feet, its broad stone-grey shield face pieced together with aged-bronze straps, fresh pale mortar, and one mismatched mossy slab. A warm lantern core glows through the carefully mended central seam as it braces across a narrow road.
1123.perspective: Low frontal three-quarter view with the full repaired construct, both feet, and patchwork shield face centered and clearly readable.
1123.background: A cool blue predawn street of pale rubble and receding scaffold poles, contrasting with the warm repairs and lantern core.
1123.notes: Bulwark reads through width and planted stance. Make repair the identity; no pristine armor, humanoid knight, weapon, giant gate, heraldry, or magical shield bubble.

1124.subject: A sturdy humanoid golem assembled from useful wreckage: one granite shoulder, one riveted iron shoulder, cedar support beams, and a bronze boiler chest lit by a warm amber core. It lifts a single broken lintel with both hands while its mismatched legs remain squarely planted.
1124.perspective: Slight low-angle full-body three-quarter view with the golem, raised lintel, and both planted feet inside the middle 70%.
1124.background: A deep cobalt-blue canvas screen and hazy teal work-yard shadow, separating the cool grey granite and iron silhouette while the warm cedar beams, bronze chest, and amber core remain distinct.
1124.notes: Bulwark is conveyed by load-bearing strength. No junk pile silhouette, giant size, weapon, extra workers, glowing runes, wheels, or chaotic scrap spikes.

1125.subject: A weathered settlement standard-bearer plants a tall repaired pole into fresh earth while unfurling a broad sun-faded cloth of warm lantern amber edged in moss green. The bearer wears practical stone-grey armor made from joined pieces and looks back toward unseen arrivals with a steady open posture.
1125.perspective: Low full-body three-quarter portrait with the bearer, entire plain banner, and planted pole centered while the cloth remains inside the frame.
1125.background: A cool blue-grey morning above half-rebuilt stone walls and thin silver mist, giving the warm banner immediate contrast.
1125.notes: The banner must be plain with no text, crest, logo, sun symbol, or nation marker. No army, victory parade, throne, weapon flourish, or battlefield corpses.

1126.subject: A broad human warden in layered iron-grey plates stands at the repaired center joint of a timber-and-stone bridge, holding a rectangular aged-bronze toll shield across the body. Moss-green ropes wrap the forearms, and a single warm lantern hangs beneath the bridge rail beside the planted stance.
1126.perspective: Eye-level full-body frontal three-quarter view with the warden, shield, bridge joint, and both boots centered and unobscured.
1126.background: A pale cold river gorge and blue-white morning mist open behind the dark armored figure, creating a clean silhouette.
1126.notes: Bulwark is quiet control of the crossing. No spear, enemy, castle gate, giant bridge panorama, readable toll sign, crest, or aggressive lunge.

1127.subject: Aric is a mature settlement leader in weathered stone-grey scale armor and a moss-green cloak, standing at ground level in the center of a circular rebuilding table rather than above it. One bare hand steadies a rough foundation model while seven mismatched bronze tools point inward around him, and a warm lantern illuminates every place equally.
1127.perspective: Medium eye-level three-quarter group-implied portrait focused on Aric and the circular table, with only cropped hands and tools of allies at the edges.
1127.background: A cool open-roof council hall of pale ruined stone under blue evening light, contrasting with the central amber lantern and bronze tools.
1127.notes: Aric must read as first among equals, not king: no throne, crown, raised dais, banner, readable plans, army, halo, or ornate regalia.

1128.subject: A lightly armored Emberward conscript vaults over a low ruined wall, carrying a short blackened-steel hook blade and a round furnace-lid buckler. Patched char-black leathers trail ember-red cloth strips, and one molten-orange boot spark marks the instant of the quick landing.
1128.perspective: Low dynamic side-on three-quarter view with the complete leaping figure, wall edge, and landing foot contained inside the middle 70%.
1128.background: A cold pale-grey training yard under blue smoke and overcast light, giving the warm cloth and sparks crisp contrast.
1128.notes: Skirmish is one short vault, not a battlefield advance. No army, giant fire trail, heavy armor, spear, heroic banner, or explosive landing.

1129.subject: A soot-streaked keeper kneels beside a waist-high bronze brazier, using long iron tongs to place one ember-red coal into a careful ring of dim cinders. A char-black apron, thick gloves, and a single gold spark emphasize patient maintenance rather than spellcasting.
1129.perspective: Eye-level medium three-quarter view with the keeper, brazier bowl, tongs, and glowing coal centered and fully readable.
1129.background: A cool blue-grey communal hall with pale stone walls and shadowed empty benches, opposing the brazier's concentrated warmth.
1129.notes: One modest civic brazier only. No bonfire, wizard staff, worshippers, forge weapon, phoenix, giant flame column, or ornate ritual symbols.

1130.subject: A broad smith-warden stands between an open forge and the viewer, wearing char-black plate with ember-red heat stains and holding a square gold-riveted hammer head downward in a resting guard. Molten-orange light leaks through the segmented visor while one gloved hand closes the furnace door behind them.
1130.perspective: Slight low-angle full-body three-quarter portrait with the warden, lowered hammer, and closing furnace door centered in the frame.
1130.background: A cold slate-blue workshop entrance and pale ash haze beyond the forge, separating the warm armor edges and furnace light.
1130.notes: Protective craftsperson, not berserker. No hammer swing, anvil explosion, towering golem scale, ornate knight heraldry, crowd, or volcanic setting.

1134.subject: A lean humanoid fire elemental strides while carrying a yoke of two differently built settlement lanterns, its body a controlled molten-orange flame wrapped in char-black iron bands and ember-red cloth ties. The two lantern flames bend toward each other and join in one gold spark above the yoke.
1134.perspective: Eye-level full-body three-quarter view with the elemental, both lanterns, and joining spark centered as a clean vertical silhouette.
1134.background: A cool blue-grey rain-dark street with pale steam rising from wet stone, opposing the warm elemental and lanterns.
1134.notes: The coalition idea is the joined lantern flames, not multiple people or flags. No wildfire, giant body, weapon, phoenix, explosive aura, or parade.

1137.subject: A veteran commander in layered char-black lamellar stands beside a disciplined waist-high signal pyre, directing its ember-red flame into one narrow horizontal beacon with a gold-bronze baton. The figure's molten-orange visor slit and squared stance convey command through control rather than fury.
1137.perspective: Low waist-up three-quarter portrait with the commander, baton, and full signal-pyre flame centered and separated from the silhouette.
1137.background: A pale cold-grey ridge under blue evening clouds, with distant rebuilding lights blurred and subordinate behind the warm focal pair.
1137.notes: No army, banner, readable insignia, throne, giant bonfire, sword flourish, roaring expression, or battlefield destruction.

1138.subject: General Kira stands as a tall adult woman formed partly from disciplined flame, her human face framed by ember-red hair that joins a compact molten-orange mantle rather than a wild blaze. Reforged char-black armor combines several repaired traditions with gold seams, and she holds a broken command blade whose two halves have just fused into one bright edge.
1138.perspective: Low medium-full three-quarter hero portrait with Kira's face, reforged blade, and complete flame mantle centered inside the middle 70%.
1138.background: A cold blue-grey assembly courtyard after rain, with pale steam and dark stone creating strong contrast around her warm unified form.
1138.notes: Fervor reads as contained forward heat in the blade and mantle. No wings, crown, army, banner, giant inferno, duplicate assassin silhouette, or cleavage-focused armor.

1139.subject: A mad-looking hermit stands atop a rock that barely breaks the water, staring at the sea and gesturing urgently. 1188.background: A deep cool slate-blue workshop floor in shadow with near-black corners.
1188.notes: Knee-high, cheap and visibly dented, earnest rather than menacing. The exposed escapement is the ticking. No weapon, no face, no glowing eyes.

1189.subject: A human-height knight built as a clock: oiled-steel plate over an open polished-brass chest cavity where a mainspring and two counter-rotating gear trains are plainly visible turning, tarnished-copper joints, and an arc-blue core burning behind the ribs. It stands squared with a plain steel longsword point-down and both hands resting on the pommel.
1189.perspective: Medium three-quarter at eye level with the knight framed from mid-thigh up and the whole head inside the image.
1189.background: A deep cool slate-blue hall receding to near-black.
1189.notes: The open, visibly working chest is what makes it clockwork rather than a suit of armour - keep those gears legible at small size. Human scale. No cape, no heraldry, no face, no glowing eyes.

1190.subject: A tall construct artificer of polished brass and oiled steel whose torso is an open workshop frame of nested gear trains, six delicate tarnished-copper manipulator arms working at once around a parchment-amber blueprint clamped across its chest. Two small arc-blue gear wisps have just spun free of its hands and hover beside it.
1190.perspective: Medium three-quarter from slightly below, the artificer large in frame from the waist up with the whole head and both wisps inside the image.
1190.background: A deep cool slate-blue workshop falling off to near-black, letting the warm brass catch all the light.
1190.notes: Exactly two small wisps - they are its work, not a swarm. The artificer is ITSELF a construct, not a person in a coat. Sizable but not a giant, and no legible lettering on the blueprint.

1192.subject: A gaunt, child-sized undead figure wrapped in a grey burial shroud, its lower face bound shut with a strip of pale linen. One thin grey hand is raised, palm out, fingers slightly spread in a hushing gesture. A single raven is caught mid-flight just beside the hand, wings frozen wide, its beak open on a cry that never finishes—a thin curl of pale mist is being drawn out of the open beak toward the wight's raised palm.
1192.perspective: Level, close three-quarter view at the wight's own small height, the raised hand and the frozen raven centred together in the middle of the frame.
1192.background: A flat, cold slate-blue graveyard mist with no headstones or ground detail, opposing the shroud's bone-grey and the mist-white thread with a single cool hue so the small silhouette stays legible.
1192.notes: The cheap, immediate half of the pair with 1193 Silent Reaper—keep this one small, quiet and still, not dramatic. No visible mouth, no glowing eyes, no runes or magic circles. The stopped raven mid-cry is the only sign anything is happening.

1193.subject: A tall, robed reaper-figure mid-stride through a wide scything sweep of a long bone-white scythe, its trailing edge already dissolving into a spreading arc of pale ash and grey moths. Two small enemy silhouettes at the far edges of the arc have their mouths and eyes fading to blank, featureless grey where the ash-moths have touched them. The reaper's own cloak and hands are visibly crumbling to the same ash from the shoulder down, already mid-dissolve as it completes the swing.
1193.perspective: Wide low three-quarter view, camera at knee height looking up along the scythe's arc, the reaper's crumbling form on one side and the ash-touched silhouettes at the far edge of frame, all inside the middle 70%.
1193.background: A dim iron-grey dusk with a faint sickly green undertone far behind, kept empty and out of focus so the pale ash arc and bone-white scythe are the brightest values in the frame.
1193.notes: The reaper dissolving as it swings IS the Toll—it only casts this on its own death, so the art should read as one continuous motion where dying and casting are the same gesture, not a healthy figure attacking. The two silenced silhouettes must stay small, generic and non-specific—not a recognisable card, just 'an enemy'. No skull face, no glowing eyes, no readable text or runes.
